scopeLabel: Source-scoped Au catalyst deposition, chemical beam epitaxy growth, composition and growth-interruption controls, catalyst-stop preparations, microscopy specimens and five single-nanowire optical contexts. All nine main pages were read in text and images. Exact physical batch identities, unlisted growth times and individual alloy line pressures remain unknown. Figure specimens are not silently joined to unreported recipes. This is not a complete laboratory SOP or a full-paper narrative Reader.

availability.morphology_illustration: Source microscopy and the original truncated-pyramid schematic are retained. A generic cylinder or sphere would misrepresent the square, tapered nanowire and embedded dot; no such finite-particle geometry is inferred. Optional bulk InP/InAs reference cells are restricted to two qualified phase contexts.

bindings.caption: Ramp the substrate from approximately 250 °C to 390 °C. Load into the Riber C-21 CBE system and ramp under TBP. Ramp duration and rate are unreported. All precursor pressures are measured gas-line pressures used as flux references, not chamber total pressure, gas dose or molar concentration. Substrate temperature is measured by pyrometer and cross-checked with the manipulator thermocouple; overall accuracy is ±10 °C. Qualified CBE chamber/substrate schematic; no unreported chamber shape, gas manifold, heater geometry or liquid reaction vessel is asserted.

Grow the InP stem for 60 min. Au-assisted VLS growth in the Riber C-21 CBE system on InP(100). All precursor pressures are measured gas-line pressures used as flux references, not chamber total pressure, gas dose or molar concentration. Substrate temperature is measured by pyrometer and cross-checked with the manipulator thermocouple; overall accuracy is ±10 °C. Qualified CBE chamber/substrate schematic; no unreported chamber shape, gas manifold, heater geometry or liquid reaction vessel is asserted.

Image the nanowires by SEM. Zeiss Merlin SEM at 5 kV; top views and side views at 45° are described in the common method. ImageJ is used for geometrical analysis. No coating, acquisition dose or exact batch ID is given. Qualified action/instrument schematic; hardware dimensions and unreported preparation settings are not inferred.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
